memory_candidates.content: A sourced guard-style shell fragment that intentionally sets a variable for the SOURCING CALLER to use after it returns (e.g. REPO_ROOT in a deploy-root-guard.sh pattern), or a caller that sets a variable only for a script it is about to source to read, triggers shellcheck SC2034 ('appears unused') because shellcheck analyzes each file independently and cannot see the cross-file read. Fix with a targeted inline `# shellcheck disable=SC2034` plus a one-line reason at the assignment site, never a file- or repo-level disable -- this is the correct, narrow remedy for genuine cross-file variable handoffs, distinct from an actually-dead variable.

To let a sourced guard script (that normally refuses non-deploy-tree invocation) self-correct for ONE specific opted-in caller without changing default behavior for the other ~58 callers: gate the self-correction on an explicit per-caller opt-in variable, attempt it only AFTER the default structural check has already failed, and accept a `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` candidate only when it passes the SAME structural test (e.g. a known directory exists directly under it) the caller's own defaults already require. This keeps every non-opt-in caller and every failed candidate byte-identical to pre-change behavior while making the guard's own final exit status 0 on acceptance, so a caller's `|| exit 1` never fires for a successful self-correction.

Some suites in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) drive many nested verify-deploy.sh --only-gate invocations and legitimately run 10-20+ minutes under run-all.sh --only. A 580s bounded-wait timeout is routinely insufficient for these; budget 1200-1800s inner timeout plus the bounded kill -0 PID-liveness waiter when verifying a phase whose dependent-suite set includes either suite.
